claims.statement: React authoring is programmatic, but its render boundary is a finite scene vocabulary.
React component state is not retained between output frames because every frame uses a fresh root that is unmounted.
Cinema retains more editorial identity and intent than Scene, while its inspector is a parallel high-level analysis path.
Cinema roles, choreography names, brand identity, and most string ids do not survive as first-class Scene fields.
Direct Scene JSON and typed Rust construction converge at the same finite Scene contract.
Layout, SVG, image, video, and timeline behavior includes destructive or materializing prepasses rather than a single immutable IR pipeline.
GPU and CPU preview can share renderer semantics with native export, but browser media resolution and scheduling keep end-to-end parity conditional.
Canvas2D is an explicit approximation and not a parity path.
Full React export materializes every evaluated frame before the native export call, creating duration-proportional scene memory and JSON I/O.
Global registries and caches require explicit isolation if authoring evaluation is parallelized or made multi-tenant.
A future CineKernel IR should preserve stable identity, semantic intent, time domains, diagnostics, and capability requirements until explicit lowering stages.
React's render and commit model is analogous only at a high level; ONDA deliberately remounts per frame rather than preserving a committed application tree.

contradictions.statement: Fresh React roots isolate host trees, but module-global active frame and depth-of-field state leave concurrent or nested reentrancy unresolved.
Renderer sharing does not imply end-to-end preview/export parity because media scheduling and fallbacks differ.
A universal Scene vocabulary is still finite and Canvas preview explicitly approximates only a subset.

hypotheses.statement: ONDA exposes more than one authoring surface.
Cinema is a semantic compiler into React rather than the renderer IR itself.
React evaluation retains component state across output frames.
All high-level Cinema identity survives lowering into Scene.
Preview and export are unconditionally identical.
Frame materialization creates a scalability risk for long React exports.
The finite primitive scene graph prevents novel visuals entirely.

primary_source_comparison.comparison: ONDA uses reconciliation to collect a host tree, but remounts each frame, so React identity and state preservation are intentionally not an output-time contract.
primary_source_comparison.lesson: Specify evaluation purity and retained-state policy explicitly.

primary_source_comparison.comparison: ONDA has several implicit levels, but most high-level semantics disappear during direct lowering rather than remaining in explicitly typed intermediate levels.
primary_source_comparison.lesson: Use staged, inspectable lowering and record semantic loss.

primary_source_comparison.comparison: ONDA export is mostly batch-oriented while GStreamer exposes pipeline direction, element boundaries, messages and clock ownership.
primary_source_comparison.lesson: Make media flow, clocks, backpressure and diagnostics first-class.
